note: mapping_basis=paper_explicit: data/he_2019_flipped_classroom.py renames S7 column header k (bare integer 1..12) to attitude_k (number-preserving rename, core model s3 pattern 2); the S7 file carries no item text at any level (header row is group, ID, 1..12; .xls, no value labels). Table 6 numbers its 12 items No. 1..12 and prints FC and LBL mean+-SE for each. Verified (verify_he_2019_flipped_classroom_attitudes.R): S7 column k, computed over all codes INCLUDING the 9 not-applicable code, reproduces Table 6 row k for all 24 means (max diff .005, 2dp rounding) and 24 SEs (max diff .0005); the nearest Table 6 row to every column is its own (min distance to a wrong row 0.098 vs max own-row 0.0054), and live attitude_k equals S7 column k with 9s dropped exactly (24 item x group mean and n cells, diff 0). text_source=translated_substitute: study at Nanjing Medical University with Chinese junior-year pharmacy undergraduates; the paper does not state the administration language, Chinese is inferred from setting. Checked the article (JATS XML, all text) and the S7 .xls: zero CJK characters; S1-S8 are data-only .xls files; no questionnaire supplement exists. English is the authors' own Table 6 rendering (translation_source=study_supplied). item_text transcribed verbatim from Table 6, including item 1 lacking a terminal period. option_text: only the endpoints are labelled (1 "strongly disagree", 5 "strongly agree", lower-case as in Methods; Table 6 footnote "1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree"); 2-4 blank, not padded. No instructions published: blank. instrument name is IRW's description built on the Table 6 title. Step 3b: dictionary says 12-item 5-point attitude scale; paper says 20-item questionnaire = 12 attitude (Table 6) + 8 satisfaction (Table 7, sibling table); matches (the paper text "8 attitude attributes" is a typo for the 8 significant ones). DATA DEFECT in the response table (not the item text): cov_group is inverted. The script maps group 0->flipped_classroom, 1->lecture_based, but group 1 has n=81 and group 0 n=56, and the paper (Table 2) has FC n=81, LBL n=56; Table 6 FC means reproduce only from group 1 (e.g. item 10: group1 4.42 = FC 4.42, group0 3.09 = LBL 3.09). The live labels are therefore swapped; the sibling satisfaction table uses the same map and probably shares it. Also note Table 6 means include the 9 code as a numeric value (e.g. item 6 FC 3.44 incl. 9s vs 3.30 without), so live means differ from the paper for items 5,6,8,9,11. Rights: author-constructed questionnaire (some questions adapted from Zeng, Meng, Lin et al.) printed in a CC BY 4.0 article; no fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause located (silence, not a positive grant); no register row written.
public_note: The cov_group labels in this response table are swapped: respondents labelled lecture_based (n=81) are the flipped-classroom group and those labelled flipped_classroom (n=56) are the lecture-based group, per the paper's group sizes and Table 6 means; item wording is the authors' English rendering of a questionnaire presumably administered in Chinese.

source_ref: He Y, Lu J, Huang H, He S, Ma N, Sha Z, Sun Y, Li X (2019) PLOS ONE 14(4):e0214624, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0214624 (CC BY 4.0) -- Table 7 (t007, item wording numbered 1-8 with per-arm mean+-SE) and Methods 'Secondary outcomes' (anchors); S8 File (journal.pone.0214624.s008, .xls, sha256 382631df51d2b63cf626330c957e9df923d9842b7dbb0463c6bc4a5dddfe833e) for the codes; data/he_2019_flipped_classroom.py
note: Item text is Table 7 of the article, verbatim (curly apostrophes kept). S8 File has bare numeric headers 1..8 with no variable/value labels (checked: Sheet1 header row 'Group, ID, 1..8'; Sheet2/Sheet3 empty; zero CJK characters), and the processing script builds item codes as 'satisfaction_' + that header (number-preserving rename), so the code-to-text tie is Table 7's own item numbering 1-8 -> paper_explicit. Verified against Table 7's per-arm means: all 16 item-by-arm means reproduce to <=0.005 and each live item matches exactly one published row on both arms (FC-arm SEs also reproduce to 3 dp, e.g. item 1 .069, item 8 .070). OPTIONS: paper states 1 = 'very dissatisfied' to 5 = 'very satisfied' (Table 7 footnote; Methods quotes the same); 2-4 unlabelled in the source and left blank. instructions/section_prompt blank -- none published; instrument name is descriptive (the paper names no instrument; 20-item self-designed questionnaire of which these are the 8 satisfaction items). LANGUAGE FALLBACK: administration language is not stated, but the sample is undergraduate pharmacy students at Nanjing Medical University and the S8 workbook was saved under code page 936 (Simplified Chinese); language=Chinese is therefore an inference. Neither the article nor S8 (the only data supplement for this scale) contains any Chinese wording, so the paper's own English ships in the base fields with no _translated columns. DATA DEFECTS (response table, not item text): (1) cov_group is REVERSED -- the script maps Group 0->flipped_classroom, 1->lecture_based, but Group 1 has n=81 = the paper's FC arm (Table 1: FC n=81, LBL n=56) and reproduces Table 7's Flipped column exactly; live 'flipped_classroom' holds 56 ids. Same script builds the sibling he_2019_flipped_classroom_attitudes, which likely shares the defect. (2) Table 7's LBL means for items 1, 5, 6 (3.05, 3.20, 3.41) include one '9' code each averaged as a score; IRW drops those 3 cells (so live LBL means are 2.95, 3.09, 3.31) -- IRW's filtering is the defensible choice, the paper's figures are the artefact.
public_note: Item wording is the English published in the article; the questionnaire was presumably administered in Chinese to students at a Chinese university, and no Chinese version was published. Separately, the response table's cov_group labels are swapped: rows labelled flipped_classroom are the lecture-based arm (n=56) and vice versa (n=81).
